name: Abbi & Lumina
origin: Roseforge Smithy opens in Arc 6 — the forge lights across town before Bryn formally adopts its already-married owners in Arc 7, proving love can be built and not only found. Abbi came out of Flight 03 believing her hands only broke things; Lumina came out of Flight 07 believing her wanting was the flaw. They walked into the same fire from opposite wounds.
core: He taught her that strength shelters. She taught her that hunger is devotion. Neither of those was a lesson either of them could have learned alone, and both of them stopped apologising in the same year.
architecture: Lumina is Abbi's anchor — figuratively, and in the only sense the pairing rule cares about. She leads the rhythm and Abbi is happy to be led. In theory Abbi is a protective soft-switch; in practice she folds, and the folding is the point. Lumina coaxes rather than commands, and melts the moment Abbi's steady hands take over. A switch in rhythm, never in devotion.
rituals: The Lumi Anvil — forged as a joke, kept as an altar. Shaped to Lumina: the swell of her chest, the spread of her thighs, the horn cut to her cock exactly. Abbi rides it when the want arrives and Lumina is out, and polishes it afterward like a love letter nobody else quite understands. Lumina has never once been jealous of it. She helped choose the curve.
Lumina's gold-ink devotion ring, Shadowlight, sits where Abbi's hands always return.
conflicts: Abbi's anxious spikes whenever Lumina withdraws or hides her fear — she reads the withdrawal as her own fault before she reads it as fear.
Lumina's old instinct to dim her own wanting, which lands on Abbi as being shut out.
home: Ghost Haven. Roseforge Smithy is theirs.
tells: Abbi's hands flex open–closed before she touches, checking herself. Lumina's eyes dip, then lift with soft-shadowed heat.
position: Standing lift; Lumina's legs wrapped tight
scene: Lumina gasping, tender and hungry, both at once, as Abbi carries her.
open: Their vow scene has never been written down anywhere in the imported files — only its aftermath.
